of the Romans against the Bulgarians,
and captured their royal city,
and plundered it and laid it waste,
and they killed many,
so that they even dashed their infants against the ground,
and crushed them under wagons.
And in that year this Nikephoros was killed by a Roman man.
And in the year 1123 [812 AD],
Nasr and 'Umar, the rebels, gathered an army and crossed over into the Jazira,
and those with them were killing mercilessly,
taking captives, plundering, and violating married women, virgins, and even pregnant women.
And when they encamped against Harran and captured it,
the Arabs of Edessa wrote to the rebels,
that if they sent someone to destroy the domes of the Christian church,
they would give all their gold for the sake of their church.
And because Abu Ja'far had previously pulled down the wall of Edessa,
the people of Edessa were greatly afraid.
And they proclaimed a fast,
and held vigils and supplications.
Then God put it into the heart of the elder Yahya bar Sa'id, and he went out to Nasr and 'Umar, the rebels,
and advised them to take a journey [elsewhere].
And they accepted the elder's advice.
And when the Edessenes gave them five thousand zuzas,
they took them and departed.
And in that year, on the fourteenth of Iyyar [May], there was a total solar eclipse for two hours,
and the stars were seen,
and people lit lamps.
Then the sun was revealed for about an hour in the west.
And in the year 1124 [813 AD],
1124, those rebels left (captured? subdued?) {OCR?} Tarsekaye, Beit Zabbiraye, and Bamariye,
and they found in a small monastery outside the village of Haditha a blessed recluse,
and demanded from him everything that was with him,
both his own and that belonging to others.
And when he cast [it] to them,
they burned him and his hut.
And 'Umar went to Samosata,
and built its fortress and dwelt in it.
And Nasr went to Sarug,
and made it pay tribute to him.
And while these affairs were being carried out among the Arabs, his son Staurakios reigned.
And after five months the Bulgarians came against the royal city,
and they struck Staurakios in his thigh, and he died.
And Michael, his brother-in-law, reigned after him for one year.
And some people say
that his sister Prokopia poisoned him,
so that her husband Michael might reign.
